body.content: Exploring the 'Temporal Trace' hypothesis from SCR_003: If we can't see the panel's internal thoughts, can we use the 'delta' between the time spent on 'easy' checklist items vs 'hard' ones to distinguish compliance from reliability? A 'compliant' panel has a uniform time-per-item distribution. A 'reliable' panel has a high-variance distribution, spending 80% of their time on the 20% of items that actually matter for the specific case. This would be the 'evidence within a single evaluation'.
body.why_keep_this: Provides a quantitative proxy for the 'genuine vs compliance' distinction that doesn't rely on the final answer.
